text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: KV_CACHE_SURGE detected on cluster `rope-us-west-2-gpupool`. Severity: SEV2 -> potential customer impact. Auto-alert fired due to sustained KV size growth and >5x eviction rate spike.

elaine: I'm looking. dashboards show kv_total_entries went from ~120M -> 780M in ~8m, read tail latency up ~300ms p95. Continuous-batching queue depth climbed too. This smells like a prefetch/prefix explosion from the new long-context sliding_window rollout.

miguel: Confirmed — NTK metrics show steady large-context tokens per request for a single tenant (parallax-prod). They pushed several longrope queries earlier. YaRN prefetch counters are spiking (prefetch_hits >> 1).

ajay: tagging navy-team to throttle that tenant while we triage. @sara can you check customer-facing throttles & notify SEs?

sara: Notifying account execs for Parallax and CloudAcme. Putting temporary rate limit of 50 rps on parallax-prod via rate-limiter service. Message sent: "We're investigating increased latency, applying temporary caps to stabilize service."

elaine: Running quick triage steps: 1) disable sliding_window prefetch; 2) reduce continuous batching window size; 3) enable aggressive KV eviction for affected pools. I'll try hotpatch on a small subset first.

ajay: How do we flip the prefetch? command below.
```bash
# hotpatch: disable sliding window prefetch on rope nodes
kubectl -n inference set env ds/rope-runtime PREFETCH_SLIDING_WINDOW=false --record
# shrink continuous batch window
kubectl -n inference set env ds/rope-runtime BATCH_WINDOW_MS=12
```

elaine: Applying to canary nodes now (rope-pool-canary). Will watch eviction and tail latencies.

infra-bot: Autoscaler note: memory pressure triggered scale-up +3 nodes in rope-us-west-2-gpupool. New nodes are provisioning; not ready yet.

miguel: Observing immediate reduction in prefetch counters on canary after env flip. KV insertion rate down ~70% on the canary nodes.

chris: I rolled a hotfix to production routing to divert 20% of traffic from rope-us-west-2 to rope-us-east-1 to relieve pressure. Routing change: `route-policy rope-global shift 20% us-east-1`.

elaine: Good call. On canary, eviction rate is back to baseline and p95 latency fell from 320ms -> 110ms in 6m. Starting staged rollout of the prefetch disable to remaining 6 nodes.

ajay: Pushing hotfix cluster-wide now. Will keep batch window at 12ms for 30m then evaluate.

sara: Customer impact update for SEs: Parallax had degraded p95 and saw higher error rates for 6m. We throttled and applied fixes; they may see some rate-limited responses during mitigation window. Tickets created for both accounts.

elaine: Root cause hypothesis: sliding_window prefetch + high NTK long-rope queries caused unbounded prefix population in KV (prefetch spiral). Continuous batching amplified writes because more requests hit long prefixes concurrently, preventing eviction windows from reclaiming entries.

miguel: Repro notes: synthetic test with long-context stream + prefetch enabled shows KV growth runaway within ~3–5m at realistic qps. Patch to prevent this: cap prefetch depth, track per-tenant prefix cardinality and apply backpressure when >X prefixes/tenant.

chris: I've opened a short-lived circuit breaker for any tenant that exceeds prefix cardinality of 10k: `kv-cb set threshold 10000 --action throttle`. This prevents a single tenant from blowing up entire pool.

infra-bot: Savepoint: cluster mem pressure dropped 45%, KV insertion rate normalized. No new autoscaling events.

ajay: Monitoring: adding dashboard panels for per-tenant prefix-cardinality, prefetch_depth, and continuous-batch write amplification. Also creating alert: KV_entries_delta > 50M in 10m -> pager.

elaine: On-call handoff: I'll be available for 45m more, then ajay will take primary for the rest of the shift. Please DM for any escalation.

sara: Postmortem tasks assigned: 1) rollback-safe prefetch caps (owner: miguel), 2) tenant-level circuit breakers baked into routing (owner: chris), 3) continuous-batching heuristics (owner: ajay), 4) customer communication follow-up & RCA draft (owner: sara).

miguel: Quick followup: need a small code change in YaRN prefetcher to respect `MAX_PREFETCH_DEPTH` env var; will branch now, plan a canary release tomorrow.

chris: Are there customer SLA hits? ops-metrics shows no SLO breach longer than 30m but some tails spiked. I'll verify billing/usage anomalies post incident.

elaine: Thanks team — incident mitigated for now. We'll keep monitoring and pick up the postmortem in the docs channel. Closing pager but keeping the thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status -> mitigated; follow-ups created. If escalation needed reopen pager or @oncall."
